meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Federal Jurisdiction, Canada - Federal corporations incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Federal common-law framework with Quebec civil law at provincial level; bijural legal system; federal corporate statutes of general application

Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force; termination notice served by China)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.4 (Individuals with Significant Control - ISC register); Canada Business Corporation Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512, ss. 21-29; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal - CBCA ISC register is maintained in corporate records but is NOT publicly searchable; access restricted to directors, shareholders (with undertakings in certain cases), CRA, FINTRAC, RCMP and other authorized authorities; publicly accessible federal beneficial-ownership registry proposed under Budget 2024 with anticipated legislative rollout for federal corporations; interim disclosure to Corporations Canada is event-driven.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) or provincial corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille - Global Affairs Canada authentication effective in Canada since 11 January 2024; foreign-origin documents must be apostilled in the country of issuance; consular legalization applies only to non-Apostille Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Corporate Profile Report for existing corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporations Canada or applicable provincial registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille - Global Affairs Canada or provincial authentication authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport, proof of residential address, and source-of-wealth statement for each director, officer, and UBO (each individual owning 25% or more or directly/indirectly controlling)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by origin-country competent authority; Canadian consular legalization only for non-Apostille jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Register of Directors (for ultimate parent entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille via origin-country competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and three recent trade references documenting project-cargo operating track record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution and principal shippers/owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for origin states; Canadian consular legalization for non-Apostille states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-closing screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, authorized signatories, material counterparties and freight-payment intermediaries against: (1) FINTRAC-conformant CDD under PCMLTFA; (2) UN Consolidated List and UN Security Council resolutions affirmed for Canada; (3) Canadian regulations adopted under SEMA, the United Nations Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (4) OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists where payment rails touch USD or US financial institutions; (5) PEP database screening with explicit enhanced-due-diligence escalation for foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates; (6) adverse-media and regulatory-enforcement checks across Canada, US, and UAE/UK registries. Red flags mandate enhanced review, including cargo-routing exposure to sanctioned jurisdictions and beneficial-ownership opacity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/121.nsf/eng/home) and NUANS Real-Time Name Search system via approved NUANS search houses
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal names may be in English, French, or bilingual (English/French). Every name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element (e.g., 'Project Cargo Heavy Haul Logistics Inc.'); only Latin-script characters are accepted, requiring transliteration of foreign-language names; 'Canadian' or 'Canada' cannot be used without demonstrating the corporation's operations are principally connected to Canada; numbered-company alternative ('-Federal Inc.') remains available where name clearance fails; maximum name length 120 characters including spaces.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director of Corporations Canada refuses a name (confusion, prohibited token, or misleading impression), the applicant may: (1) file a revised NUANS report with a new distinct name (within 90 days of the original search); (2) submit a written reconsideration request with supporting consent letters from holders of prior marks/professional regulators to the Director within 30 days of refusal; (3) where consent or disclaimer cures confusion, refile via the online system with an attached consent; (4) appeal to the Federal Court by notice of application for judicial review under s. 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act within 30 days of the Director's final decision; (5) preserve rights by filing Articles of Incorporation with a numbered name while seeking a later formal change of name. A new NUANS search is mandatory if the original report is more than 90 days old.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual/registered-agent office is generally accepted by Corporations Canada for the CBCA registered office as long as service of process is reliably available at a physical address in the designated province; however, for a project-cargo logistics entity the following physical-substance caveats apply: (a) commercial banks and project lenders ordinarily require a physical principal office for account opening and LC issuance; (b) customs brokers/carrier bonds and CBSA-related filings may require a Canadian place of business; (c) extra-provincial registration is triggered once the corporation carries on business in a province; recommendation is a serviced office in the operating province (Ontario/Quebec) with executed mail-forwarding and process-agent agreements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk (approximately 5%): routine unannounced physical inspections of the registered office are not conducted by Corporations Canada; on-site verification is triggered principally upon FINTRAC compliance examination, CRA audit, or evidence of registered-office irregularities; probability increases to approximately 15-20% if the corporation engages in customs-related bonds or becomes an approved importer, given CBSA program integrity visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 5 (Articles of Incorporation), s. 8 (Pre-Incorporation Contracts), s. 101 (Registered Office), s. 106 (Directors), s. 128 (Shares), s. 114 (Bylaws), and s. 252 (Regulations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), Government of Canada.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001 under the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001), submitted via the Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; the corporation may incorporate with zero authorized paid-up capital. Shares may be issued for cash, property, or past services; no escrow or capital deposit account is mandated by the federal regulator.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the directors named in the Articles of Incorporation are elected to hold office until the next annual meeting of shareholders. That the registered office of the Corporation shall be located at the address set forth in the Articles, in the Province of Ontario, Canada. That the subscribers shall subscribe for and the Corporation shall issue the authorized common shares upon payment of nominal consideration. That the Corporation's by-laws be adopted as presented. That the following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary. That management is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, appoint signatories, and register with the Canada Revenue Agency for the Business Number, GST/HST, and payroll accounts to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada via an approved NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) service provider or the ISED portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary search with the proposed corporate name 'PROJECT CARGO HEAVY HAUL INC.' (or alternative). File the name reservation request stating the ISIC 5229 freight arrangement business purpose. Retain the NUANS report (valid for 90 days) and attach the result reference to the subsequent incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and 3 alternate names
Consent to use name from any individual named in the corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is confusingly similar to an existing trademark or corporation, amend the proposed name to a distinct variation and resubmit; the statutory review period restarts upon refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, Directorate of Corporations, ISED.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001 (Articles of Incorporation) designating the registered office address, the number and classes of directors (minimum one), share structure (unlimited common shares), and any restrictions on share transfers or business activities. Submit electronically through the Online Filing Centre with payment of the CAD 200 government fee. Receive the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Director consent forms (Form 4005 or in-articles consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Articles contain deficiencies, Corporations Canada issues a Notice of Deficiency; cure by amending the Articles via a supplementary filing or correcting the electronic form and refiling within 60 days to preserve the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada registration records; provincial registry (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery) for operational presence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office address stated in the Articles is a physical location in Canada where records may be accessed. Appoint a records office if different from the registered office. Notify Corporations Canada of any change using Form 4003 within 15 days of the change.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership evidence of registered office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is invalid (e.g., a P.O. Box without a civic address), substitute a valid physical civic address and file an address change notice to maintain statutory service capacity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, By-laws, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal governance; no governmental clearance required).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting or execute unanimous written resolutions in lieu of a meeting. Adopt the general operating by-law, fix the fiscal year-end, approve the share subscription, issue share certificates, and appoint the initial officers as set out in the first board resolution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory records (minute book, share register, directors' register) are incomplete, rectify by convening a subsequent board meeting and ratifying the defective resolution retroactively, subject to unanimous shareholder consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Program Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a federal Business Number (BN) and program accounts, including GST/HST (RT account), corporate income tax (RC account), and payroll deductions (RP account) if employees will be engaged. Use the BN for all customs, excise, and import/export filings relevant to project cargo logistics.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the incorporation particulars, reconcile the legal name and BN against the Federal Corporate Registry; apply for account re-opening or correction of the program account within 30 days of the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial corporate registries in each province of operations (e.g., Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the federal corporation extra-provincially in every province where it establishes a physical office, warehouse, or solicits business, filing the applicable provincial registration form (e.g., Ontario Form 2 – Initial Return) and paying the provincial fee. Obtain municipal business licenses for each office location.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Municipal business license application and fee
Registered office address in the province
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a province rejects the extra-provincial filing due to name conflict, apply to the provincial registry for an assumed name registration (alternative name) and forward the approval to Corporations Canada.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada, Motor Carrier Safety Division, and provincial motor carrier boards (only if the corporation later operates its own heavy-haul fleet; not required for freight arrangement and project logistics brokerage activities).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No federal sectoral operating license is required for ISIC 5229 freight arrangement. Contingent license: Extra-Provincial Operating License (Motor Carrier Rights) under the Motor Vehicle Transport Act, 1987, required only where the entity owns and operates out-of-gauge heavy-haul vehicles.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (CEPA) registry.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Registration Only. Office-based freight arrangement and logistics coordination services have no physical industrial facility, manufacturing, or land-altering activities; no Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) screening or comprehensive study is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to head-office administration. If the corporation later owns vehicles, compliance with Transport Canada's on-board diagnostic and GHG emission standards (CMVSS), provincial idling controls (e.g., Ontario Highway Traffic Act s. 178.1), and CEPA Part 5 thresholds for volatile organic compound (VOC) releases apply; waste handling must follow provincial hazardous waste regulations with generator registration where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and occupancy permit from the applicable municipal fire marshal for the head office; structural load clearance for any project cargo warehousing or staging yard leased by the corporation; workplace safety compliance under the Canada Labour Code, Part II (if federally regulated employer) or provincial Workers' Compensation Board coverage (e.g., WSIB in Ontario) for all employees; first aid, hazardous materials handling (TDG/ADR training), and forklift/heavy equipment operator certification where staging operations are performed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — National e-portal: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO), retrieved via canada.ca/revenue-agency; GST/HST NETFILE for registrant filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign corporation must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) through the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal (Form RC1 / RC1A) by providing legal name, articles of incorporation, Canadian agent or place of business, and corporate status documents. The BN with Program Code 'RT' constitutes the GST/HST registration number; Program Code 'RM' is used for an Import/Export (Customs) account. Registration is mandatory once taxable supplies made in Canada exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; voluntary registration is recommended from day one for a project-cargo logistics carrier with milestone billing, as it permits input tax credits and clean zero-rated export treatment of outbound heavy-haul services.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential banking supervision by Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/ATF transaction reporting by Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII and applies no exchange-control licensing or central bank approval for CAD conversion. Funds may be freely repatriated as dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, or capital reductions, subject to Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (statutory 25%; treaty-reduced, including 5% or 15% under the Canada-US tax convention depending on ownership and residency). Profit remittance documentation generally requires audited or reviewed financial statements, tax residency certificates, and treaty benefit forms where applicable. No FX conversion license or prior monetary authority authorization is required for non-resident shareholders or project cargo operators.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no deadline for converting foreign currency receipts into CAD. Exporters may retain export earnings offshore or onshore in any currency. Compliance documentation is required by Export Development Canada (EDC) and federal customs reporting (B13 export declaration) for financing or statistical purposes, but there is no central-bank surrender obligation. FINTRAC large-transaction reporting and record-keeping duties may apply if export payments involve cash or certain equivalents above statutory thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Ancillary multi-currency settlement — Medium; primary CAD treasury — Low. A non-resident offshore EMI or e-money institution cannot lawfully accept deposit liabilities in Canada unless authorized as a bank or authorized foreign bank under the Bank Act. It may register with FINTRAC as a money service business (MSB) for transmission services, but it cannot provide CDIC-insured CAD accounts, direct Payments Canada clearing, or a complete treasury foundation for federal corporate tax/payroll. The viable structure is a Schedule I bank as the primary CAD operator, with a regulated foreign EMI used only for OECD WH/European/US disbursement nodes and lower-value project cargo operating expenses in EUR/USD/GBP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian federal law does not require a director to appear physically in a bank branch. Remote account opening is permitted by most Schedule I banks for a Canadian federal corporation, provided FINTRAC-compliant electronic identity verification is satisfied, corporate registry data from Corporations Canada is verified, and source-of-funds evidence is provided. In practice, banks often require a live video interview for non-resident directors and may require notarized identification, apostilled corporate documents, or a Canadian legal opinion. A fully remote non-resident-controlled treasury account is feasible but easier with an existing banking relationship or Canadian counsel sponsorship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner in a jurisdiction with limited FATF equivalence or high corruption risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full passport copies; tax residency certificates; notarized personal KYC forms; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; international bank reference letters; corporate registry extracts; UBO register; independent negative media/AML screening report; Canadian legal opinion confirming beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cargo routing to, through, or near sanctioned or transshipment-risk territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global Affairs Canada export permit or confirmation of non-controlled status; CBSA declaration; B13 export documentation; end-user and end-use certificates; INCOTERMS 2020; full voyage/route plan; vessel and aircraft clearance documentation; cargo insurer lists; project employer letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large milestone wires for OOG heavy-haul services without a clear underlying trade contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed project cargo logistics agreement; heavy-haul tariff and rate card; commercial invoices; purchase orders; freight forwarding contracts; vessel booking confirmations; road/rail/port access permits; project master schedule; milestone certification reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid disbursement of injected capital immediately after bank onboarding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving treasury operations; detailed 12-month cash-flow forecast; escrow instructions; existing vendor and subcontractor contracts; equipment lease agreements; terminal and port rental confirmations; tax and payroll obligations schedule; explanation of the heavy-haul project ramp-up.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in federal share structure or intercompany funding through shareholder loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporations Canada annual return; certified shareholder ledger; share subscription agreements; loan facility agreements; arm's-length interest-rate supporting evidence; contemporaneous board minutes; Part XIII withholding analysis; financial statements and accountant confirmation of debt-to-equity position.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Canadian Schedule I bank beneficiary account, quoted with the full CAD account format: 5-digit branch transit, 3-digit institution number, and account number. Remittance purpose must state clearly 'equity subscription and paid-in capital contribution for Canadian project cargo heavy-haul operations' to satisfy FINTRAC record-keeping and bank AML screening. Verification pack: bank account opening KYC, corporate resolution approving capital injection, source-of-wealth disclosures for each funding shareholder, share subscription agreement, and updated shareholder register. CAD high-value settlement clears through the Bank of Canada high-value payment system/Lynx network if required; foreign currency conversion may be executed at bank spot or via a pre-agreed forward rate. No central-bank permit is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border vendor payments to ocean carriers, port terminals, heavy-lift vessel brokers, subcontractors, and equipment lessors, with invoice and project references in field 70. For high-value engineered equipment or contractual milestones, issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700 (MT707 for amendments) subject to UCP600, with presentation documents including commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, and inspection certificate. USD disbursements clear through Fedwire/CHIPS, CAD through Lynx, EUR through TARGET2/Single Euro Payments Area equivalents; all payments must be matched against the approved vendor KYC profile, signed contracts, INCOTERMS 2020, and customs/export control documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forward (vanilla single currency)
FX swap / swap-roll for short-dated CAD-USD or CAD-EUR treasury matching
Cross-currency swap for CAD/USD/EUR project debt or capital account exposures
Vanilla FX option and zero-cost collar
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) only for non-convertible route-market currencies with documented underlying exposure; not required or appropriate for CAD/USD
Board-approved ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with a Schedule I Canadian bank, limited to hedging actual project cargo or treasury exposures, with no speculative open positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return and Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Director under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days following the anniversary date of incorporation; no extension permitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs administrative surcharge; the Director of Corporations Canada may dissolve the corporation if the annual return is delinquent for two consecutive years (s.212 CBCA); reinstatement requires court order or Director approval with additional fees and compliance costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's taxation year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty under s.162(1) of the Income Tax Act: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delinquency (maximum 12 months), escalating to 10% for second/third violations; interest charged under s.161; unpaid tax may be registered as a lien and director liability may apply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (where the corporation is an annual remitter)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three months after the end of the GST/HST fiscal year (e.g., March 31 for calendar-year corporate filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the amount owing plus 1% per month of delay (up to 12 months); daily compound interest on overdue balances; habitual failure may trigger CRA audit and administrative enforcement action

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all CBCA corporations unless the corporation is not a distributing corporation and all shareholders pass a unanimous resolution to dispense with an auditor (s.156 CBCA); distributing corporations (publicly listed or with public share distribution) can never waive the audit requirement, and within two months after each annual meeting an auditor must be appointed
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for distributing corporations; ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for non-distributing private enterprises; corporations may also elect IFRS voluntarily

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under s.21.1 CBCA, every corporation must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISCs), updated within 15 days of any change, including share transfer events; the annual return filed with Corporations Canada must confirm current ISC information and provide a snapshot of the register as at the anniversary date; materially false or incomplete ISC disclosure is a strict-liability offence on directors
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

stage_6.entry_description: Legal entity name and 9-digit Business Number with program identifier RC0001; full registered office address.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada must file T2 and identify the Canadian permanent establishment; registered office may be in Canada through an agent.
